if (v.lockedUntil != 0 && block.timestamp < v.lockedUntil) revert VaultLocked();

note: Marked redundant because it could not be reached. `test_lockedVault_refusesTheRequestAndPaysOutOnlyAfterMaturity` pins the reachability argument and starts failing at its first line if the lock ever comes off the request path. The lock stays on the request. `WITHDRAW_TERM_TERM` is 0, which does not disturb the argument, because it rests on time being monotonic from the request to the execution and not on any gap between them: a same-block execution has the request's own timestamp, which the request already proved was at or after `lockedUntil`.
proof: Unreachable. The lock is checked twice on the queued path, and the first check is the binding one: `requestWithdraw` runs `_requirePersonalWithdrawer`, which reverts `VaultLocked` on exactly this condition (UL-01). `lockedUntil` is written once, in `createVault`, and no path writes it again, so it is fixed for the life of the record. `executeWithdraw` settles a request that `requestWithdraw` already created, so its block timestamp is at or after the request's. A request that got through therefore proves `block.timestamp >= lockedUntil` at the request, and monotonic time carries that to every later execution: `block.timestamp < v.lockedUntil` cannot hold here.
